his47.name: his version of the SSRI paragraph (card SC-47), links put back
his47.text: Why Standard Meds Failed You If you have tried SSRIs (antidepressants) and failed, you are not crazy. In a small trial of male combat veterans with severe, long-term PTSD, Prozac did no better than a placebo (Hertzberg, et al, 2000). Trials in veterans have been mixed since, yet the VA still recommends sertraline and paroxetine (VA/DoD, 2023). And the side effects are well-known, including anhedonia, zombification, and sexual dysfunction.

his48.name: his version of why the drugs fail (card SC-48), typos and links fixed
his48.text: Why don't these drugs work on calcified PTSD? Because even if they did work for mood by modulating serotonin transmission, PTSD is not a mood disorder. That's a bit like putting some Bengay on a broken leg. This protocol tries to get at the underpinnings of the problem. The ketone BHB blocks enzymes called HDACs (Shimazu, et al, 2013), and in mice that couldn't hold on to extinction learning (learning that a cue is now safe), an HDAC blocker made the new learning last (Whittle & Singewald, 2014). Whether ketosis does that in people hasn't been tested.

his50.name: his version of the Fix (The Unlock) (card SC-50), links put back
his50.text: The Fix (The Unlock): DeltaFosB does fade on its own, but slowly, and the same fears keep making more. Along with therapy and the de-armoring supplements, we use "System Reformats" (Psychedelics and Iboga). Iboga raised GDNF, a growth factor that protects dopamine neurons, in rats (He, et al, 2005), and one dose of psilocybin grew new connections in mouse brains that lasted a month (Shao, et al, 2021). Whether either loosens DeltaFosB's hold hasn't been tested directly, although these have been shown to help with addictions, which DeltaFosB plays a role in.

his51.name: his new paragraph on strains, parasites and toxins (card SC-50), typo and links fixed
his51.text: While the science is focused on some specific substances in certain psychedelics, like psilocybin and ibogaine, the reality is much more complicated. Each iboga tree and each mushroom strain (and phenotype) have different levels of different psychedelic alkaloids apart from the principal ones studied. You can learn more about the different types of iboga in my iboga guide. Aside from the different ibogas, I find loveyhuasca to be more clear-headed than shrooms and often more beneficial, although some shroom strains, like Orissa India, are much more therapeutic than others (like Golden Teacher, Penis Envy) in my experience. And part of the way these help, from my understanding, is their antiparasitic action. Each psychedelic, and even each mushroom strain seems to target a different subset of parasites, and there's an anecdote-based theory that physical parasites solidify mental and spiritual ones. I remember eating some B+ strain shrooms which people told me were very mild and gentle. For me it was the opposite, absolute hell, until a very large and strange parasite came out and then instantly I felt amazing. More recently, I've learned that the toxins released during the psychedelic parasite cleanse actually block a lot of the benefits that we can get from the experience. Binding those toxins or protecting the brain from them is crucial for max benefits. I explain my methods for doing so in my Altered States Guide.
